target.title: fix(plugin-sdk): update ssrf-runtime import path in cdp-proxy-bypass
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Packaged OpenClaw can fail while lazy-loading the bundled Browser plugin or Ollama embedding provider because their compiled output retains an import of `openclaw/plugin-sdk/ssrf-runtime-internal`. That private subpath is intentionally excluded from the published package, so source-checkout tests can pass while the installed package fails at runtime.

Fixes #96639.

## Why This Change Was Made

The original PR promoted privileged local-origin and proxy-bypass helpers into the public plugin SDK. The maintainer refactor keeps the existing private owner boundary and fixes the packaging layer instead: the unified tsdown graph always bundles the exact internal SSRF self-import used by the bundled Browser/Ollama owners. Public `ssrf-runtime` remains unchanged.

## User Impact

- Packaged Browser and Ollama code can lazy-load without a missing private-subpath error.
- External plugins do not gain new privileged SSRF/proxy APIs.
- Source-checkout behavior and public SDK imports remain unchanged.

## Evidence

- Blacksmith Testbox `tbx_01kx381a0wnbaw3nv1eq10tqct`: 149/149 focused Browser, Ollama, and tsdown-config tests passed.
- The same Testbox completed a full `pnpm build`, including tsdown, SDK declaration generation, export checks, postbuild, and Control UI build: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29012934667
- Fresh autoreview reported no actionable findings (correctness confidence 0.93).
- `oxfmt` and `git diff --check` passed.
- Exact-head CI: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29013257015

## Test Plan

- [x] Preserve private `ssrf-runtime-internal` imports for bundled owners.
- [x] Force that exact self-import into the unified build graph.
- [x] Prove the public SSRF runtime is not force-bundled or widened.
- [x] Run focused Browser/Ollama/build-config regression suites.
- [x] Run a full distributable build.

Original implementation and diagnosis by @pengxuewu-lab.
